paragraphs.title: Kish, Saul, and the Search for the Donkeys

easy.explanation: Saul was the son of Kish.
easy.q: Who was Saul’s father?

easy.explanation: Kish’s asses, or donkeys, were lost.
easy.q: What had been lost?

easy.explanation: Kish told Saul to take one of the servants.
easy.q: Whom did Kish tell Saul to take with him?

answers: He feared his father would worry about them
medium.explanation: Saul feared that his father would stop caring for the donkeys and worry about them.
medium.q: Why did Saul suggest returning home?

answers: Mount Ephraim, Shalisha, Shalim, and the land of the Benjamites
medium.explanation: They passed through these regions while searching for the donkeys.
medium.q: Which places did Saul and his servant pass through before reaching the land of Zuph?

answers: He was a notable and capable man
medium.explanation: The phrase presents Kish as a prominent and capable man.
medium.q: What does the description “a mighty man of power” suggest about Kish?

challenge.explanation: Saul was concerned that his father would worry about him and the servant.
challenge.q: What quality of Saul is shown when he is willing to stop searching?

answers: He was older than all Israel
challenge.explanation: The description emphasizes Saul’s impressive appearance, not an existing kingship.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Saul being described as choice, goodly, and taller than the people?

answers: The donkeys were lost, Saul searched for them, and then he suggested returning
Saul met Samuel, and then the donkeys were lost
Kish found the donkeys, and then sent Saul
challenge.explanation: This is the order given in the passage.
challenge.q: What is the correct sequence of events?

short_answers.question: What did Saul search for?
short_answers.explanation: Kish sent Saul to seek the asses.

short_answers.question: Who went with Saul?
short_answers.explanation: Kish told Saul to take one servant with him.

short_answers.question: Why did Saul want to return?
short_answers.answer: He feared his father would worry about them.
short_answers.explanation: Saul said his father might stop caring for the donkeys and take thought for them.

paragraphs.title: The Attendant Suggests Consulting the Man of God

easy.explanation: The servant suggested going to the man of God in the city.
easy.q: To whom did the servant suggest they go?

answers: The fourth part of a shekel of silver
easy.explanation: The servant had a quarter shekel of silver.
easy.q: What did the servant have with him?

easy.explanation: The passage says that a prophet was formerly called a seer.
easy.q: What was a prophet formerly called?

answers: They had no present to bring him
They did not know the way
medium.explanation: Saul said their bread was spent and they had no present to bring.
medium.q: Why did Saul hesitate to go to the man of God?

answers: He offered the quarter shekel he had
He asked Kish for more money
He offered one of the donkeys
medium.explanation: The servant offered the silver he had at hand.
medium.q: How did the servant solve the problem of the present?

medium.explanation: A present is a gift brought to a person.
medium.q: In this passage, what is a “present”?

answers: The servant offered a practical solution
challenge.explanation: The servant’s offer of silver removed Saul’s concern about bringing a present.
challenge.q: What persuaded Saul to accept the servant’s suggestion?

answers: He was famous only for his wealth
challenge.explanation: The servant regarded his words as reliable and certain.
challenge.q: What does the servant’s statement that all the man of God says comes surely to pass show?

answers: Seer was an earlier name for a prophet
A seer was a prophet’s servant
Seer was the name of the city
challenge.explanation: The text explains that a prophet was formerly called a seer.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between “seer” and “prophet” in these verses?

short_answers.question: Who suggested visiting the man of God?
short_answers.explanation: The servant proposed that they go to the man of God.

short_answers.question: What did Saul lack for a present?
short_answers.answer: He had no gift to bring.
short_answers.explanation: Saul said there was no present to bring to the man of God.

short_answers.question: What did the servant offer?
short_answers.answer: A fourth part of a shekel of silver.
short_answers.explanation: He offered the silver he had at hand.

paragraphs.title: Meeting the Young Women and Finding the Way to the High Place

easy.explanation: They were going out to draw water.
easy.q: What were the young women doing?

easy.explanation: They asked whether the seer was there.
easy.q: Whom did Saul and his servant ask about?

easy.explanation: The people were gathering for a sacrifice and meal.
easy.q: What was going to take place at the high place?

answers: The people had come to the city for a sacrifice
The city was about to close
medium.explanation: They said there was a sacrifice of the people that day in the high place.
medium.q: Why did the young women tell Saul and his servant to make haste?

answers: They would find the seer before he went to the high place
They would find Kish by the well
They would have to return home
medium.explanation: The women said they would find him before he went up to eat.
medium.q: What would Saul and his servant find if they went up into the city?

answers: A raised place where the sacrifice and meal were held
medium.explanation: It was the elevated place where the sacrifice and meal took place.
medium.q: What is the high place in this context?

answers: They gave directions and explained why they should hurry
They searched for the donkeys with them
challenge.explanation: They told them where the seer was and why he would soon go to the high place.
challenge.q: How did the young women help Saul and his servant?

answers: The seer had an important role in the meal
The people did not know the seer
challenge.explanation: The people waited for him to bless the sacrifice.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the people waiting to eat until the seer came?

answers: Saul asked the young women, they answered, and directed him toward the city and high place
The young women ate, and then Saul questioned them
Samuel questioned the women, and then Saul arrived
challenge.explanation: This is the order of the encounter in the passage.
challenge.q: What is the correct sequence?

short_answers.question: What were the young women doing?
short_answers.explanation: Saul and his servant met them as they went out to draw water.

short_answers.question: Where was the seer going?
short_answers.explanation: The women said he would go up to the high place to eat.

short_answers.question: Why would the people not eat until the seer came?
short_answers.explanation: The passage says the people waited because he blessed the sacrifice.

paragraphs.title: The Lord Prepares Samuel for Saul

easy.explanation: The LORD told Samuel about Saul the day before he came.
easy.q: To whom did the LORD reveal Saul’s coming?

easy.explanation: The man would come from the land of Benjamin.
easy.q: From which tribe would the man come?

answers: Be captain over Israel and save the people from the Philistines
easy.explanation: Samuel was to anoint him captain, and he would save Israel from the Philistines.
easy.q: What was the man appointed to do?

answers: At the end of the month
medium.explanation: The LORD said, “To morrow about this time.”
medium.q: When did the LORD say the man would come?

answers: The cry of the people had come unto the LORD
medium.explanation: The LORD had looked upon His people because their cry had come to Him.
medium.q: Why would the man save Israel?

answers: He privately revealed information to Samuel
medium.explanation: The expression means that the LORD revealed the matter to Samuel beforehand.
medium.q: What does “told Samuel in his ear” mean?

answers: His coming was presented as part of the answer to Israel’s distress
He came only to eat at the meal
challenge.explanation: The LORD said Saul would save His people from the Philistines.
challenge.q: How is Saul’s coming connected with Israel’s trouble?

answers: Saul is the man about whom the LORD had spoken
Saul is one of the servants
challenge.explanation: The LORD identifies Saul as the man Samuel had been told about.
challenge.q: What becomes clear when Samuel sees Saul?

answers: Captain over Israel and deliverer from the Philistines
challenge.explanation: The LORD had already revealed Saul’s future role to Samuel.
challenge.q: What role is described for Saul before Saul knows about it?

short_answers.question: What was Samuel to do to the man from Benjamin?
short_answers.answer: Anoint him to be captain over Israel.
short_answers.explanation: The LORD told Samuel to anoint him as captain.

short_answers.question: What danger would Saul save Israel from?
short_answers.explanation: The LORD said Saul would save His people from the Philistines.

short_answers.question: What did the LORD say Saul would do over His people?
short_answers.explanation: The LORD identified Saul as the man who would reign over His people.

paragraphs.title: Saul Meets Samuel and Receives a Hint of His Destiny

easy.explanation: Saul asked Samuel to tell him where the seer’s house was.
easy.q: What did Saul ask Samuel?

easy.explanation: Samuel identified himself as the seer.
easy.q: Who told Saul, “I am the seer”?

easy.explanation: Samuel told Saul that the lost donkeys had been found.
easy.q: What did Samuel say about the donkeys?

answers: To the high place to eat with him
medium.explanation: Samuel told Saul to go up before him to the high place and eat with him.
medium.q: Where did Samuel invite Saul to go?

answers: Israel’s desire would be connected with them
His family had lost its standing
medium.explanation: Samuel asked whether all Israel’s desire was not upon Saul and his father’s house.
medium.q: What did Samuel hint about Saul and his father’s house?

answers: The valued or desired position in Israel
medium.explanation: The phrase points to honor, importance, and what Israel desired.
medium.q: What does “all the desire of Israel” mean in this context?

answers: With joy only because the donkeys were found
challenge.explanation: Saul emphasized that Benjamin was small and his family was the least.
challenge.q: How did Saul respond to Samuel’s hint?

answers: He did not see himself as worthy of such greatness
He already viewed himself as king
He thought he was above all Israel
challenge.explanation: Saul described himself as belonging to a small tribe and an insignificant family.
challenge.q: What does Saul’s answer reveal about how he viewed himself?

answers: Samuel hints at greatness, while Saul emphasizes his family’s smallness
Samuel speaks about donkeys, while Saul speaks about the meal
Samuel is angry, while Saul laughs
challenge.explanation: Samuel points toward honor, but Saul responds with humility and astonishment.
challenge.q: What contrast appears between Samuel’s words and Saul’s response?

short_answers.question: What did Samuel say had happened to the donkeys?
short_answers.explanation: Samuel told Saul not to set his mind on the donkeys because they were found.

short_answers.question: What did Samuel say about Israel’s desire?
short_answers.answer: It was upon Saul and his father’s house.
short_answers.explanation: Samuel hinted at Saul’s future importance.

short_answers.question: How did Saul describe Benjamin?
short_answers.answer: As one of the smallest tribes of Israel.
short_answers.explanation: Saul called himself a Benjamite of the smallest tribes.

paragraphs.title: The Meal and the Special Honor Given to Saul

answers: In the chiefest place among the guests
easy.explanation: Samuel made them sit in the chiefest place among those invited.
easy.q: Where did Samuel seat Saul and his servant?

easy.explanation: Samuel told the cook to bring the portion reserved for Saul.
easy.q: For whom had Samuel ordered the special portion?

easy.explanation: The passage says Saul ate with Samuel.
easy.q: With whom did Saul eat that day?

answers: He brought out the shoulder and placed it before Saul
He returned it to the kitchen
He gave it to the servant
medium.explanation: The cook took up the shoulder and set it before Saul.
medium.q: What did the cook do when Samuel requested the portion?

answers: Samuel had commanded that it be reserved
The young women had requested it
medium.explanation: Samuel had told the cook beforehand to set it aside.
medium.q: Why had the portion been kept?

answers: A place of honor among the guests
medium.explanation: It was the most honored place at the meal.
medium.q: What does “the chiefest place” mean?

challenge.explanation: The honored seat and reserved portion show special treatment.
challenge.q: What does seating Saul in the chiefest place show about Samuel’s attitude toward him?

answers: Why he was receiving such special honor
challenge.explanation: Saul had not yet understood the reason for Samuel’s unusual honor.
challenge.q: What had Saul not yet understood at the meal?

answers: Both point to Saul’s future special status
Both prove the donkeys were not found
challenge.explanation: The hint and the honored place both suggest Saul’s importance.
challenge.q: How does the honor at the meal connect with Samuel’s earlier hint?

short_answers.question: Where did Samuel seat Saul?
short_answers.answer: In the chiefest place among the guests.
short_answers.explanation: Samuel gave Saul the place of honor.

short_answers.question: What portion was set before Saul?
short_answers.answer: The shoulder and that which was upon it.
short_answers.explanation: The cook brought the reserved portion and placed it before Saul.

short_answers.question: Who ate with Saul?
short_answers.explanation: Saul ate with Samuel that day.

paragraphs.title: The Rooftop Conversation and the Promise of God’s Word

answers: On the top of the house
easy.explanation: Samuel communed with Saul upon the top of the house.
easy.q: Where did Samuel speak with Saul after the meal?

answers: At the spring of the day
Only at the end of the meal
easy.explanation: Samuel called Saul early in the morning, at the spring of the day.
easy.q: When did Samuel call Saul?

easy.explanation: Samuel told the servant to pass on before them.
easy.q: What did Samuel tell the servant to do?

answers: So Samuel could show Saul the word of God privately
So the servant could find the donkeys
So he could prepare the meal
medium.explanation: After the servant went ahead, Samuel could speak privately with Saul.
medium.q: Why did Samuel tell the servant to go ahead?

answers: He went with Saul toward the end of the city
He returned to the high place
medium.explanation: Samuel and Saul went abroad together toward the end of the city.
medium.q: What did Samuel do before speaking privately with Saul?

answers: Samuel was about to reveal God’s message to Saul
Samuel would teach Saul a song
Samuel would tell Saul where the high place was
medium.explanation: Samuel was preparing to disclose a message from God.
medium.q: What does “I may shew thee the word of God” mean?

answers: Samuel was preparing Saul to receive an important personal message
Samuel wanted to avoid speaking with Saul
Saul wanted to return home immediately
challenge.explanation: Samuel kept Saul with him and arranged a private moment for God’s word.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the move from the rooftop to a private place outside the city?

answers: He moves from searching for donkeys to receiving God’s word
challenge.explanation: At the end, Saul is about to receive an important message from God.
challenge.q: How does Saul’s role change by the end of the chapter?

answers: Conversation on the rooftop, departure at dawn, the servant goes ahead, and preparation to reveal God’s word
The servant goes ahead, then the meal, the search for donkeys, and the rooftop conversation
They leave the city, return to the rooftop, and then meet the young women
challenge.explanation: This is the sequence described in the final verses.
challenge.q: What is the correct sequence at the end of the chapter?

short_answers.question: Where did Samuel speak with Saul after they came down from the high place?
short_answers.answer: Upon the top of the house.
short_answers.explanation: Samuel communed with Saul on the rooftop.

short_answers.question: When did Samuel and Saul leave?
short_answers.answer: At the spring of the day, or dawn.
short_answers.explanation: They arose early and went out together.

short_answers.question: What did Samuel intend to show Saul?
short_answers.explanation: Samuel asked the servant to go ahead so he could reveal God’s word to Saul.
